**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:23399)

**Proposed mechanism:** FREM1 (HGNC:23399) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization and cell adhesion (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization and cell adhesion (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal lacrimal system morphology (HP:0000524); Extracellular matrix organization and cell adhesion (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal hair morphology (HP:0001072); Extracellular matrix organization and cell adhesion (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Anal atresia (HP:0002046). Loss-of-function mutations in FREM1 disrupt extracellular matrix organization and cell adhesion processes, leading to a spectrum of developmental defects including abnormal lacrimal system morphology, abnormal hair morphology, and anal atresia, which manifest as the distinct phenotypes of the two diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in FREM1 with a gain-of-function or dominant-negative mechanism for either disease would falsify this hypothesis. This could involve gene therapy or small molecule approaches to restore protein function or modulate downstream pathways.
